title: Monroy wins women's one-meter title as Gators advance multiple finalists at Tennessee Invite
text:
Anthony Nesty, Head Coach at Florida Gators Women's Swimming & Diving | https://floridagators.com/
Anthony Nesty, Head Coach at Florida Gators Women's Swimming & Diving | https://floridagators.com/
Florida Gators divers began the Tennessee Diving Invitational in Knoxville with a strong showing, highlighted by a win in the women's one-meter event. Florida’s Monroy secured first place in the women’s one-meter final with a score of 309.95.
The Gators had seven athletes reach the finals on Wednesday at the Allan Jones Aquatic Center, with all four women advancing in the one-meter competition. Fung posted a career-best score of 291.30 during preliminaries to qualify as the second seed for the finals, while Monroy entered as third seed with a 283.05.
In addition to Monroy's victory, another Gator took third place in the women's one-meter (279.35). Brinkman finished 11th after scores of 222.10 in prelims and 233.25 in finals, while Greenberg placed 12th overall.
On the men’s side, Agundez led Florida’s three-meter prelims with a score of 366.30 and later finished third in the finals (406.30). Gesing placed eighth in the finals after scoring 361.50, having led Gators’ efforts earlier in prelims as well.
Other performances included seventh and ninth place finishes from additional Florida divers, and a fifteenth-place finish rounding out their squad.
Head Diving Coach commented on the team's performance: "Excellent first day today. The competition here is some of the best we will see all season. At SECs and NCAAs. There is usually some rust after our winter break but they didn't show much of that today. Camyla is getting back to championship form and Alexa continues to raise her level each meet. The men's contest was extremely high level and Agundez put himself in position to win going into the last round. He was off just a little bit today but next time he won't be. Conor also showed signs of his old form and will definitely be sharp in the championships. Great first day for the Gators!"
Competition continues Thursday with men's one-meter and women's three-meter events beginning at 11 a.m., followed by finals scheduled for later that afternoon.
